newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mixed, bears eye natgas, weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mixed, bears eye natgas, weather.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were mixed Monday in quiet trade, but mild East Coast weather and cratering gas prices roused more bearish sentiment, industry sources said.

"The weather is not supportive, and with natgas plentiful and getting cheap, oil is going to have to compete again," said one cash trader, noting players also were concerned about Star's coker maintenance this month that was cranking out 50,000 barrels per day of extra U.S. Gulf high sulphur.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent remained quoted at about $18 a barrel, traders said.
NYH Feb one percent paper eased slightly to the high-$17 area, with March paper down a quarter to $17.50-75.

NYH 0.3 percent high pour firmed 25 cents to $19.75 after recent utility interest, while low pour edged up to $21.75 or higher on reports of a 100,000-barrel sale late Friday at $22 (Feb 12-17 delivery).
High sulphur in New York mostly eased slightly, with three percent now straddling $16 on concerns about U.S. Gulf refinery unit outages that were boosting HS supply.
At the U.S. Gulf, one percent was unchanged at $16.50, while three percent slipped a quarter to $14.25-50 on reports of two sub-$14 sales Friday for small prompt pieces.
New York city gate gas prices tumbled another 30-40 cents to the low-$3.00/mmBtu area on mild weather in the region. NYH one percent resid remained at a $2.85/mmBtu equivalent.
